'''''Disphyma crassifolium''''', commonly known as '''round-leaved pigface'''<ref name="ABRS">{{cite web |last1=Venning |first1=Julianne |title=''Disphyma crassifolium'' |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Disphyma%20crassifolium |publisher=Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of Agriculture, Water and the Environment: Canberra |accessdate=16 October 2020}}</ref> or '''salty fingers'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://totallywilduk.co.uk/2022/02/01/salty-fingers-id-guide/|title=Salty Fingers (Disphyma crassifolium) Identification}}</ref> is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Aizoaceae]] native to Australia and the [[Cape Provinces]] of South Africa. It is a [[Prostrate shrub|prostrate]], [[succulent plant|succulent]] [[Annual plant|annual]] shrub or short-lived [[perennial plant]] with stems up to {{cvt|2|m}} long, leaves that are three-sided in cross-section with a rounded lower angle, and purple daisy-like flowers with [[staminodes]] up to {{cvt|30|mm}} long.

==Description==
''Disphyma crassifolium'' is a prostrate, succulent, annual or short-lived perennial shrub that typically grows to a height of {{cvt|2–30|cm}} and has stems up to {{cvt|2|m}} long. Its leaves are club-shaped, more or less round to three-sided in cross-section, {{cvt|5–70|mm}} long and {{cvt|1–7|mm}} wide. The flowers are {{cvt|20–50|mm}} wide with a [[perianth]] tube {{cvt|6–12|mm}} wide, the longer lobes {{cvt|2-30|mm}} long with purple, petal-like [[staminode]]s {{cvt|110–30|mm}} long that are white on the lower surface. Flowering mainly occurs from October to February and the fruit is a conical [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]] that is about {{cvt|10|mm}} long and wide before opening.<ref name="ABRS" /><ref name="FloraBase 2799">{{FloraBase | name = ''Disphyma crassifolium'' (L.) L.Bolus | id = 2799}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Disphyma crassifolium'' was first published in 1753 as ''Mesembryanthemum crassifolium'' by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in ''[[Species Plantarum]]'' from species collected in southern Africa.<ref name=APNI1>{{cite web|title=''Mesembryanthemum crassifolium''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/602630 |publisher=APNI|accessdate=17 October 2020}}</ref><ref name="L.">{{cite book |last1=Linnaeus |first1=Carl |title=Species Plantarum |date=1753 |page=484 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/84235#page/492/mode/1up |accessdate=17 October 2020}}</ref><ref name="Haworth1">{{cite book |last1=Haworth |first1=Adrian H. |title=Miscellanea Naturalia, sive Dissertationes Variae ad Historiam Naturalem Spectantes |date=1803 |publisher=J. Taylor |location=London |page=78 |url=https://archive.org/details/miscellaneanatu00hawogoog/page/n84/mode/2up |accessdate=17 October 2020}}</ref> In 1925, [[Nicholas Edward Brown]] raised the genus ''[[Disphyma]]'' in ''[[The Gardeners' Chronicle]]''<ref name=APNI2>{{cite web|title=''Disphyma''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/488030|publisher=APNI|accessdate=17 October 2020}}</ref> and in 1927 [[Harriet Margaret Louisa Bolus]] moved Linnaeus's ''M. crassifolium'' into the new genus as ''Disphyma crassifolium'' in the botanical magazine ''[[Flowering Plants of South Africa]]''.<ref name=APNI3>{{cite web|title=''Disphyma crassifolium''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/511948|publisher=APNI|accessdate=17 October 2020}}</ref>

In 1803, [[Adrian Hardy Haworth]] described ''Mesmbryanthemum clavellatum'' in his book ''Miscellanea Naturalia, sive Dissertationes Variae ad Historiam Naturalem Spectantes'' from plants raised from seed collected in Australia by [[Robert Brown (botanist, born 1773)|Robert Brown]].<ref name="Haworth2">{{cite book |last1=Haworth |first1=Adrian H. |title=Miscellanea Naturalia, sive Dissertationes Variae ad Historiam Naturalem Spectantes |date=1803 |publisher=J. Taylor |location=London |page=79 |url=https://archive.org/details/miscellaneanatu00hawogoog/page/n84/mode/2up |accessdate=17 October 2020}}</ref> In 1976, [[Robert Chinnock]] moved ''M. clavellatum'' to the genus ''Disphyma'' as ''D. clavellatum'' in the ''[[Royal Society Te Apārangi|New Zealand Journal of Botany]]''.<ref name=APNI4>{{cite web|title=''Disphyma clavellatum''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/511927|publisher=APNI|accessdate=17 October 2020}}</ref><ref name="Chinnock">{{cite journal |last1=Chinnock |first1=R. J. |title=Studies in Disphyma — a genus related to Mesembryanthemum: 2. Infraspecific subdivision of Disphyma australe and notes on the Australian species of Disphyma |journal=New Zealand Journal of Botany |date=March 1976 |volume=14 |issue=1 |page=78 |doi=10.1080/0028825X.1976.10428653}}</ref> Then, in 1986, [[John Peter Jessop]] reduced ''Disphyma clavellatum'' to a subspecies, [[Disphyma crassifolium subsp. clavellatum|''Disphyma crassifolium'' subsp. ''clavellatum'']] in ''Flora of South Australia'',<ref name=APNI5>{{cite web|title=''Disphyma crassifolium'' subsp. ''clavellatum''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/511982 |publisher=APNI|accessdate=17 October 2020}}</ref> a name accepted by the [[Australian Plant Census]] and [[Plants of the World Online]].<ref name=APC1>{{cite web|title=''Disphyma crassifolium'' subsp. ==Distribution and habitat==
''Disphyma crassifolium'' is widely distributed in South Africa and Australia. It grows in saline areas such as coastal dunes and samphire flats, and tolerates a range of soils including sand, loam and clay.<ref name="ABRS" /><ref name="FloraBase 2799"/>
